findings:
🟠 [errexit-leak] MUST-FIX The frame-parse block does `set +e` … `set -e`, but the script runs under `set -uo pipefail` with errexit deliberately off; the trailing `set -e` turns errexit ON for everything after it (codex hardened checks, containment/identity compare, emit_result/trap paths), so any bare non-zero command in those later paths now aborts with an unmapped exit code instead of the documented status table. Impact: silent behavior change outside the touched branch. Remediation: delete both `set +e` and `set -e` and just read `PARSE_RC=$?` after the awk (no errexit was active to disable).
🟠 [codex-gate-mismatch] MUST-FIX The prompt wrap is gated on `RUNNER != codex`, but the completion predicate is gated on `CODEX_TRANSPORT != 1`. For `--runner codex` without the transport env, no frame is injected (BEGIN/END/DERIVED empty) yet the locator still runs and always ends with `!started` → `frame_missing`/exit 5; conversely a non-codex runner with `CODEX_TRANSPORT=1` gets a wrapped prompt but no strip, so consumers receive a framed artifact. Spec item 2 scopes the predicate to "non-codex runners". Remediation: gate the predicate block on the same condition as the wrap (`[[ "$RUNNER" != "codex" ]]`, optionally `&& -n "$BEGIN"`).
🟡 [forbidden-scan-narrowed] MUST-FIX `validate_json_result` now passes only the last `^{` line to the Python checker instead of the full `$out`, so the endpoint-URL/token forbidden-substring scan no longer covers stderr/other stdout lines for cases 1–3 (spec: never weaken an existing assertion). Remediation: keep the forbidden-value scan over the full `$out` and only use `json_line` for `json.loads`; if non-JSON lines newly appear in `$out`, name the source in a comment.
🔵 [dead-close-file] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `FRAME_CLOSE_FILE` is created, written by awk, and immediately removed without being read; harmless leftover from the copied locator, remove when the shared lib is extracted.
🔵 [report-md-note] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Spec asks that the locator duplication and the dispatch-plan-review.js carry-through be named in REPORT.md; the diff puts both in the script header only. Not a runtime defect; REPORT.md is outside the reviewed diff.
